newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sentiment to improve in June BOJ tankan--report.
newsitem.headline: Sentiment to improve in June BOJ tankan--report.

text.p: The Bank of Japan's (BOJ) "tankan" survey of short-term corporate sentiment, due on June 25, is likely to show a better business outlook than the previous survey in March, Tokyo-Mitsubishi Securities Co said in a report on Friday.
The report said the business diffusion index, a key gauge of corporate sentiment, is expected to improve to plus four among major manufacturing firms from plus two in the previous survey.
The index for major non-manufacturing firms is projected at minus four, compared with minus six in the March survey.
When the BOJ released its March tankan, it forecast the June index would be minus one among major manufacturers and minus seven among major non-manufacturers.

The report also said the tankan is expected to show that major Japanese firms plan to increase their capital spending by 6.2 percent in the current business year to March 31, 1998, compared with an increase of 2.7 percent predicted in the previous survey.
Tokyo-Mitsubishi also said the BOJ is likely to raise the official discount rate by 0.5 percentage point to one percent in the October-December quarter of this year.
"The BOJ is unlikely to make a hasty decision to raise the discount rate as it will be assessing economic developments after the (April 1) increase in the sales tax," it said.
The report added that it could not deny the possibility of an early rise in the discount rate if the United States raises interest rates or if the yen weakens further against the dollar.
